post_text:
We chose strict, schema-first API contracts over dynamic JSON payloads when building our core payment gateway.

The team wanted the flexibility of schemaless documents to move fast, and I felt like an outdated gatekeeper for blocking them.

I spent nights worrying that my insistence on rigid Protobuf schemas and strict validation rules would slow us down to a crawl.

The developers complained about the extra compilation step, and I quietly questioned if I was just clinging to old habits out of fear.

Two years later, a downstream team refactored their entire database schema and accidentally changed a critical field type from integer to string.

Our strict API gateway rejected the very first malformed payload at the edge, preventing corrupted data from silently poisoning our ledger.

We did not have to run a single recovery script or explain a balance discrepancy to our customers. The boring, rigid contract did its job without anyone needing to wake up at 3:00 AM.

That assumption costs more than latency.

What I learned:

Strict API contracts are a thankless insurance policy that pays out when you least expect it.
